terms.gloss: boundary, frontier; in the plural, territory

evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.132: contentiō dē terminīs (Lewis & Short)
Lewis & Short s.v. attingō: “to lie near, border upon, be contiguous to”
Traupman 202: at the boundary between Italy and Switzerland, ad discrīmen Ītaliae et Helvētiae
terms.comment: The classical sense is “that which divides”, hence a distinction or a crisis; Traupman uses it of a boundary line.

phrases.latin: Hīc Pȳrēnaeī montēs, in cōnfīniō Hispāniae et Galliae
phrases.english: Here are the Pyrenees, on the border between Spain and France
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

phrases.english: on the east it is bounded by
at the boundary between Italy and Switzerland

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Lewis & Short: finis
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 202, 319.
